Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum.
It was first released in 1991 and emphasizes code readability and simplicity.

Python supports multiple programming paradigms including procedural, object-oriented,
and functional programming. It has a large standard library and a vibrant ecosystem
of third-party packages available via PyPI.

Common uses of Python include:
- Web development (Django, FastAPI, Flask)
- Data science and machine learning (NumPy, Pandas, PyTorch, TensorFlow)
- Scripting and automation
- Scientific computing

Python uses indentation to define code blocks, which enforces a consistent coding style.
The Python Software Foundation (PSF) manages the language's development and licensing.
